item.text:
**3B.4 Note**
Best read: **partial internal complaint/discipline machinery exists, but Xi did not build independent civilian oversight or credible external investigation systems for abuse.** The 2024 record shows complaint portals and Party-state inspection bodies, plus elite purges, but these are internal controls, not independent due process.

| Assessment | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Partial positive | `12389举报投诉平台` | PRC Ministry of Public Security | 2024 | https://12389.mps.gov.cn/clue_reportNotice.action | The MPS maintains a public complaint/reporting portal for police misconduct. This is a real complaint channel, but it is internal to the security apparatus, not an independent civilian oversight body. | `3B.4`, `3B.2` |
| Partial positive | `公安机关督察条例` | PRC public security authority text / local government repost | 2024-02-01 | https://gaj.cq.gov.cn/zwgk/zfxxgkml/zcwj/xzfg/202402/t20240201_12890414.html | The regulation creates an internal police inspectorate that can hear public complaints, respond to ongoing illegal conduct, and correct or revoke police decisions. This is oversight in form, but it stays inside the police chain of command. | `3B.4`, `3B.2` |
| Partial positive | `中央纪委国家监委通报2024年上半年全国纪检监察机关监督检查、审查调查情况` | CCDI / National Supervisory Commission | 2024-07-25 | https://www.ccdi.gov.cn/toutiaon/202407/t20240725_363777.html | The Party-state discipline system reported 47.7 million complaint-type reports in H1 2024 and 40.5 million case filings. That shows heavy complaint intake and investigation capacity, but it is Party discipline, not independent civilian oversight or judicial review. | `3B.4`, `2B.9` |
| Partial positive | `The Politburo approved Li Shangfu’s expulsion from the Party` | Xinhua | 2024-06-27 | https://www.xinhuanet.com/20240627/f929f9248c9f40bc8f9afe791c6a716f/c.html | A politically protected defense-ministry figure was investigated and expelled. This shows elite discipline can be enforced, but it is corruption/discipline enforcement, not independent investigation of abuse or due process for victims. | `3B.4`, `2B.9` |
| Strong negative | `Hong Kong: No Accountability 5 Years after Mass Protests` | Human Rights Watch | 2024-06-10 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/10/hong-kong-no-accountability-5-years-after-mass-protests | HRW says the government offered no accountability for police abuses and that Hong Kong lacked an independent mechanism for police complaints. This is direct evidence against credible civilian oversight. | `3B.4`, `3B.1`, `3B.2` |
| Strong negative | `2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: China` | U.S. Department of State | 2025-08-12 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128572.html | The report says China had credible reports of arbitrary killings, disappearances, torture, and arbitrary detention, and that the government took no credible steps to punish abusers. This strongly undercuts any claim of an effective independent investigation system. | `3B.4`, `3B.1`, `3B.2` |

**Synthesis**
- **Answer:** mostly **No**.
- Xi’s system in 2024 had **internal reporting and discipline channels**, and it sometimes reached politically protected elites.
- But I found **no credible evidence of independent civilian oversight**, external complaint adjudication, or genuinely autonomous investigation of abuse by police, intelligence, prisons, or party enforcers.
- The strongest positive items are **internal to the Party-state**, which is not the same as due process or independent review.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a 2024 source showing Xi created or tolerated an **independent** complaints body with real power over police/security abuse.
- I also did not find evidence that complaint mechanisms were insulated from political control when politically protected actors were involved.
